function.mechanism: Acts as a mineral flow aid that reduces powder caking and as an alkaline buffering agent that neutralizes acidity; can also function as a processing/handling aid.
common_food_categories: General direct food uses under cGMP

adi.basis: A dedicated accessible EFSA food-additive re-evaluation opinion for E504 was not retrieved in this run (EFSA search endpoint blocked; historical call URL archived/moved).

efsa.key_finding: OpenEFSA contains a magnesium carbonate substance entry (including E 504(i) alias), but accessible linked output retrieved was feed-additive workflow, not a food-additive E504 re-evaluation opinion.

adi.basis: INS 504(i): NOT LIMITED (1965). INS 504(ii): NOT SPECIFIED (1979), included in ADI for other hydrogen carbonates.

concerns.summary: At higher medicinal exposures in renal-risk populations (e.g., dialysis), magnesium carbonate-containing regimens can cause hypermagnesemia requiring dose adjustment or discontinuation in some cases.
High supplemental/medicinal magnesium salt intake can cause gastrointestinal adverse effects (notably diarrhea); magnesium carbonate is among forms associated with this effect.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA lists magnesium carbonate as GRAS as a direct human food ingredient under 21 CFR 184.1425 with cGMP limitation.
JECFA ADI outcomes are non-numeric permissive categories (NOT LIMITED for INS 504i and NOT SPECIFIED for INS 504ii).
No magnesium carbonate-specific IARC classification entry was identified on the IARC agents-classified page reviewed.

populations: People with impaired renal function at high magnesium intakes
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI (mg/kg bw/day) was identified for E504 from accessible regulatory records; concern is primarily high total magnesium exposure from medicinal/supplement sources rather than typical food-additive use.

risk_assessment.rationale: Accessible regulatory sources show permissive status at food-use levels (FDA GRAS, JECFA non-numeric ADI categories), while observed adverse effects are mainly dose-dependent and concentrated in vulnerable renal populations or medicinal-use contexts.
key_factors: FDA GRAS listing with cGMP condition (21 CFR 184.1425)
JECFA ADI: NOT LIMITED (504i) and NOT SPECIFIED (504ii)
No identified IARC classification entry for magnesium carbonate
Hypermagnesemia and GI effects are documented mainly at higher clinical/supplemental exposures
